assigned: BEFORE the S9 power simulation was run and without any market data; scores come from the stated reasons only. They are not edited after the simulation.

hypotheses.name: Lottery-demand avoidance (MAX effect)
hypotheses.mechanism: behavioural: retail demand for lottery-like payoffs overprices coins with extreme recent single-day gains; they earn lower subsequent returns

reasons.economic_plausibility: a named behavioural mechanism with an observable proxy; crypto spot is retail-heavy; the literature is NOT verified in this environment, so this is a hypothesis, not a fact
reasons.research_feasibility: needs only point-in-time daily closes (available); cross-section N >= 40 from 2021 (S1 counts); detection power limited like every candidate
reasons.implementation_simplicity: one formula, one fixed window, no fitted model, ranks only
reasons.expected_practical_value: weekly rebalance gives high turnover (cost-sensitive) and a long-only portfolio captures only the avoid-the-lottery half of the spread

hypotheses.name: Post-listing hype decay (listing-age filter)
hypotheses.mechanism: supply/novelty: newly listed coins attract attention and are overpriced relative to their later cash-flow-free fundamentals; the premium decays with age

reasons.economic_plausibility: the mechanism is plausible but age also proxies size, liquidity and survival, so the signal is hard to separate from known confounds; listing date is the Binance listing, not the coin's true age
reasons.research_feasibility: few young coins at any date and the skill would be concentrated in them, so the cross-sectional test has a small effective sample
reasons.implementation_simplicity: no price calculation; needs only the point-in-time listing date
reasons.expected_practical_value: lowest turnover, nearly cost-insensitive, but it acts more like a universe filter than an alpha source

hypotheses.name: Illiquidity compensation (Amihud)
hypotheses.mechanism: liquidity risk premium: investors demand compensation for holding assets that are costly to trade; illiquidity measured as mean absolute return per unit of quote volume

reasons.economic_plausibility: a standard risk-compensation mechanism, distinct from behavioural ones; untested in this environment
reasons.research_feasibility: needs daily close and quote volume (available); same cross-sectional power as the others
reasons.implementation_simplicity: one formula, one fixed window, ranks only
reasons.expected_practical_value: the premium sits in the least liquid quintile where slippage, capacity, minimum notional and delisting risk are worst; the assumed cost per trade is most likely understated there
